sample.title: Sample tour
sample.summary: A short tour used to test the tour engine.

welcome.title: Your apps
welcome.body: Every app you use lives in this bar.

postMessage.title: Post a message
postMessage.body: Write a message and send it.

liveTicket.title: A ticket arrives
liveTicket.body: Watch a new ticket come in.

ticketsInbox.title: Your tickets
ticketsInbox.body: Tickets from your customers land here.

autoplayFixture.title: Autoplay fixture
autoplayFixture.summary: Drives each kind of input autoplay supports.

mention.title: Thank someone
mention.body: Write a message that mentions a teammate.

session.title: Steer a session
session.body: Write an instruction for the session.

status.title: Change the status
status.body: Open the status menu and pick a status.

threads.title: Messages and agents
threads.summary: Post in a conversation, speak instead of typing, and bring an agent in with @.

messages.title: Your conversations
messages.body: Messages holds your conversations with your team and your agents. Open one to follow along.

post.title: Post a message
post.body: Write a message in the box at the bottom and send it. If I write it for you, read it over and press Send yourself.
post.text: Hello everyone, I'm trying out Liaison.

dictation.title: Speak instead of typing
dictation.body: When dictation is on for your workspace, press the microphone and talk. Your words land in the box, cleaned up.

mentionAgent.title: Bring an agent in
mentionAgent.body: Type @ and pick an agent, then say what you need, and send. The agent joins the conversation. If I write it for you, press Send yourself.
mentionAgent.text: can you sum up this conversation?

agentAnswers.title: The agent answers here
agentAnswers.body: Its reply arrives in this conversation, like a teammate's. You can keep talking to it.

attach.title: Add files
attach.body: Use + to attach a file or a screenshot to your message.

agents.title: Agents and approvals
agents.summary: Meet your agent, ask it something, and see how it checks with you before it acts.

profile.title: Your agent
profile.body: This agent works for you, with your access and nothing more.

capabilities.title: What it can do
capabilities.body: These are the kinds of things it can read and do for you.

ask.title: Ask it something
ask.body: Open a conversation with your agent and ask a question.
ask.text: What can you help me with?

asksFirst.title: It asks before it acts
asksFirst.body: Before it sends an email or changes something that matters, the agent asks you first.

approvals.title: Your requests
approvals.body: Everything waiting for your decision is listed here.

decide.title: Decide
decide.body: Read what it wants to do, change it if needed, then approve or decline. Nothing happens until you do.

routines.title: Routines
routines.summary: Let your agent do recurring work on a schedule or when something happens.

tab.title: Routines
tab.body: Routines are tasks your agent runs by itself, on a schedule or when something happens.

list.title: Your routines
list.body: Each routine shows when it runs and how its last run went. Pause one at any time.

templates.title: Ready-made routines
templates.body: Your apps suggest routines. Turn one on to start from it.

create.title: Create a routine
create.body: Give it a name and say what to do. It starts as a personal routine.
create.name: Morning summary
create.text: Each morning, tell me in a few lines what is waiting for me today.

activity.title: See every run
activity.body: Activity shows what your agent did, routine runs included.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.summary: Run the coding agent on a computer you paired, and steer it while it works.

list.title: Your sessions
list.body: A session is the coding agent working in a folder on one of your computers.

computers.title: Your computers
computers.body: Paired computers show here. To pair one, install the desktop app and sign in. No computer yet? You can skip the next step.

start.title: Start a session
start.body: Say what you want done, pick a folder, then press Start. This needs a paired computer: without one, skip this step.
start.text: Look around this project and tell me in a few lines what it does.

steer.title: Steer it
steer.body: Open a session and write here to change course while it works.

status.title: When it needs you
status.body: The header shows what the session is doing and tells you when it is waiting for you.

basics.title: Mail basics
basics.summary: Your agent sums up a conversation and drafts the reply, you approve it.

inbox.title: Your inbox
inbox.body: Mail from your mailboxes lands here, personal and shared.

open.title: Open a conversation
open.body: Click a conversation to read it, then press Next.

summariseDraft.title: Ask for a summary and a draft
summariseDraft.body: Open your agent from Chats, beside the conversation, and ask it to sum up the thread and draft a reply. Nothing is sent: the draft waits in the conversation for you.
summariseDraft.text: Sum up this conversation for me and draft a reply.
summariseDraft.phoneText: Sum up my newest unread email conversation for me and draft a reply.

approve.title: Review and approve
approve.body: Read the draft, edit it if needed, then press Approve: approving sends the reply. If I do it for you, I press Approve on this draft.

crm.title: Who is writing
crm.body: The customer card shows what your other systems know about the sender. Your agent reads it too.

yourself.title: You can also write yourself
yourself.body: You can reply here, or start a new email, whenever you prefer to write it yourself.

basics.title: Tickets
basics.summary: Your agent drafts the reply and the note, you review and approve.

inbox.title: Your tickets
inbox.body: Requests from your customers land here as tickets.

open.title: Open a ticket
open.body: Click a ticket to open it, then press Next.

customerCard.title: Who the customer is
customerCard.body: The customer card shows what your other systems know about this customer. Your agent reads it too. On a phone, it is under More.

askDraft.title: Ask your agent for a draft
askDraft.body: Open your agent from Chats, beside the ticket, and ask it to draft a reply. It reads the ticket, the customer's record and their past tickets. Nothing is sent: the draft waits on the ticket for you.
askDraft.text: Draft a reply to this customer. Use what we know about them: the ticket, their customer record, their past tickets and our knowledge base.
askDraft.phoneText: Draft a reply to my newest open ticket. Use what we know about the customer: the ticket, their customer record, their past tickets and our knowledge base.

review.title: Review and approve
review.body: The draft is on the ticket. Read it, edit it if needed, then press Approve: approving sends the reply to the customer. If I do it for you, I press Approve on this draft.

note.title: Ask for a note for the team
note.body: In your agent's conversation, ask it to sum up the case in an internal note and press Send. Only your team sees it.
note.text: Add an internal note to this ticket that sums up the case for the team: what the customer asks and what we already know.
note.phoneText: Summary for the team: what the customer asks and what we already know.

approveNote.title: Approve the note
approveNote.body: Your agent read about the customer before writing it, and some people who read this ticket cannot see that, so it asks you first. Read the note in the conversation and press Approve. If I do it for you, I press Approve on this note.

yourself.title: You can also do it yourself
yourself.body: You can write a reply or a note yourself here whenever you prefer.

routine.title: On every new ticket
routine.body: A routine can ask your agent for this on every new ticket: a note and a reply draft. You still read and approve every reply before it goes out.

basics.title: Knowledge
basics.summary: Where your company knowledge lives and how to add to it.

home.title: Your knowledge
home.body: Documents your team and your agents rely on live here.

collections.title: Collections
collections.body: Documents are grouped in collections and folders.

create.title: Add knowledge
create.body: Your agent opens and helps you write a document from a page, a file or your notes. Tell it what to use.

recent.title: Recently touched
recent.body: The documents changed lately show up here. Open one, then press Next.

edit.title: Edit a document
edit.body: Open a document you can edit, press Edit, change the text and save.

share.title: Who sees it
share.body: Choose who can read or edit this document.

agents.title: Your agents use it
agents.body: When your agents answer, they read the documents you can see and say where the answer came from.

basics.title: Projects
basics.summary: Your agent plans a project with its tasks, you review it and comment.

home.title: Your projects
home.body: Each project holds its tasks, its board and its discussion.

askPlan.title: Ask your agent for a plan
askPlan.body: Open your agent from Chats and ask it to plan the work as a project. It creates the project and its tasks for you.
askPlan.text: Plan our autumn webinar series as a new project: create the project with one task for each step, in one go.

approvePlan.title: Approve the project
approvePlan.body: Your agent asked before creating the project and its tasks: it read things some people who see projects cannot. Its card lists every task; read it in the conversation and press Approve.

review.title: Review the plan
review.body: Your agent's project is in the list. You can open it and check its tasks (edit, reorder or delete any of them), then press Next.

comment.title: Comment on a task
comment.body: Open one of its tasks, write a comment under it and press Send.
comment.text: Looks good. I'll take this one.

yourself.title: You can also do it yourself
yourself.body: You can assign a task, give it a due date or add a task by hand whenever you prefer.

settings.title: API connector
settings.summary: Your connections to your own systems, how to test them, and asking your agent about a customer.

page.title: Your connections
page.body: Each connection links Liaison to one of your systems, such as a CRM or an ERP.

connections.title: Status and roles
connections.body: Each connection shows whether its key works and what it provides, such as customers or orders.

test.title: Test a read
test.body: Press Test on a connection, pick a read, fill in its fields and run it.

result.title: The result
result.body: You see the answer's status, how long it took and the rows it returned.

add.title: Add a connection
add.body: Press Add connection, paste the adapter file and save, then enter its key.

ask.title: Ask your agent about a customer
ask.body: Open your agent from Chats and ask what a customer ordered. It reads your CRM or ERP through the API connector and answers with what it found.
ask.text: Use the API connector to read our CRM or ERP: which customer ordered most recently, and what did they order?

card.title: Where it shows up
card.body: The same reads fill the customer card on tickets and mail, so your team and your agent see the customer's orders where they work.

engine.waiting: Waiting for this step to be done. It moves on by itself.
engine.playing: Playing this step for you. Move the mouse or type to take over.
engine.takeover: You took over. Finish this step yourself, or let me do it again.
engine.autoplayFailed: I could not find what this step needs on screen, so I stopped.
engine.autoplayRefused: This step did not look as expected, so I stopped before doing anything. Do it yourself, or skip it.
engine.agentFailed: Your agent could not finish this step, so it will not move on by itself. Try again, or skip it.
engine.agentNoAnswer: Your agent could not answer, so this step will not move on by itself. Try again, or skip it.
engine.anchorWaiting: Waiting for this to appear on screen.
engine.requestFailed: That did not go through. Try again.
engine.noTours: No tours for the apps in this workspace yet.
engine.watching: Watching for this to happen. It moves on by itself.
engine.gateVerify: Confirm your email to continue: this step runs an agent.
engine.gateBudget: The demo budget is used up, so this step cannot run.
engine.gateFailed: This step did not go through.

welcome.agentsBody: Your demo is ready. Confirm your email so the agents can work, then pick where to start.
welcome.codeLead: Enter the code from your email
welcome.ownKey: Use your own model key instead
welcome.chooseTitle: Where do you want to start?
welcome.confirmed: Email confirmed. Your agents can run.
welcome.ownKeyReady: Your own model key is saved. Your agents can run.
welcome.startOverBody: Your workspace goes back to its starting state: the mails, approvals and records made so far are gone, and your scenarios go back to 0/{{n}}. Your demo budget and its end date stay the same.
welcome.startOverOwnKey: Your own model key stays with this workspace: add it again in the new one.
welcome.startOverFailed: That did not go through. Try again.

engine.agentAnswered: Your agent answered without doing this step. Reply to it in the conversation (for example "go ahead"), try again, or skip this step.
engine.agentWaiting: Your agent has not done this yet. It may have asked you something in the conversation: answer it there, try again, or skip this step.
engine.workingAgent: Your agent is working on it. This step moves on when its answer is here.
engine.heldBody: Your agent asks before it uses {{tool}}. Read its card and press Approve to continue.
engine.workingRoutine: The routine is running. This step moves on when it has finished.
engine.routineNotStarted: The routine has not started. Skip this step to go on.
engine.workingReplay: The recorded session is playing. This step moves on when it gets there.
engine.routineRunning: The routine “{{name}}” is working on it ({{elapsed}}). This step moves on when it is done.
engine.routineRunningUnnamed: The routine is working on it ({{elapsed}}). This step moves on when it is done.
engine.routineFailed: The routine “{{name}}” stopped with an error: {{error}} Try again later, or skip this step.
engine.routineFailedUnnamed: The routine stopped with an error: {{error}} Try again later, or skip this step.
engine.routineFailedNoReason: The routine “{{name}}” stopped with an error. Try again later, or skip this step.
engine.routineFailedNoReasonUnnamed: The routine stopped with an error. Try again later, or skip this step.
engine.routineSkippedNoReason: The routine “{{name}}” did not run this time. Skip this step, or try it again later.
engine.routineSkippedNoReasonUnnamed: The routine did not run this time. Skip this step, or try it again later.

common.undoRole: Every action you approve waits a few seconds before it really happens, so a slip is one click to take back.
common.railHome: Open Home on the left bar
common.railTickets: Open Tickets on the left bar
common.railProjects: Open Projects on the left bar
common.railChats: Open Chats on the left bar
common.railMail: Open Mail on the left bar
common.railAgents: Open Agents on the left bar
common.railShopify: Open Shopify on the left bar
common.railInvoicing: Open Invoicing on the left bar
common.railSessions: Open Sessions on the left bar
common.railKnowledge: Open Knowledge on the left bar
common.sendBelow: Send the question below with Send
common.openRunConversation: Open your conversation with {{agent}}, at the top of Chats

held.title: Your agent asks before it writes
held.body: Your agent read outside content earlier in this conversation (a web search, for example) or data not everyone can see, so it asks before it writes. Read its card and press Approve to continue.
held.role: This is configurable: an admin can set approval policies. The globe beside your agent's name shows the mark; click it and choose Clear the mark to lift it.
held.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to see the action come back as a request.
held.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen

common.railStripe: Open Stripe on the left bar

support.title: Support
support.summary: A customer writes in; the support routine posts a note and a reply draft; you review and approve.

inbox.title: Your support inbox
inbox.body: Let's watch one come in: press Next.
inbox.role: You run support. Every customer request lands here as a ticket, and a routine reads each one as it arrives.

liveTicket.title: A customer is writing in
liveTicket.body: Nothing to do yet: her ticket lands at the top of the list in a moment. Press Next once it is there.
liveTicket.role: Lena Hart's Kestrel 10 stopped charging after an update, and she is emailing support about it right now.

open.title: Her ticket is here
open.body: Open her ticket, then press Next.
open.role: Before anyone answers Lena, you want to see what she wrote.
open.way2: Click Lena Hart's ticket, at the top of the list

approve.title: Approve the reply
approve.body: Edit a sentence if you like, then press Approve. It goes to Lena (a fictional customer here).
approve.role: You decide what goes out: read the draft as Lena will read it.
approve.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to see the reply come back as a draft.

sent.title: Sent
sent.body: The reply shows in the conversation, next to the routine's note. Press Next.
sent.role: Lena has her answer, and the team can see exactly what was said.

askAgent.title: Check whether Lena is a VIP
askAgent.body: Ask {{agent}} from Chats, beside the ticket, and press Send. It answers from her tickets and her customer record.
askAgent.text: Is Lena Hart a VIP customer? What has she bought from us, and what did she report before?
askAgent.role: Before you promise Lena a replacement, you want to know if she is a VIP customer and what she reported before.

answer.title: Its answer
answer.body: {{agent}} answers beside her ticket, from her tickets and customer record. Press Next once it has answered.
answer.role: You decide on the replacement with her history in front of you.
answer.way3: Read its answer under your question

done.title: That's support
done.body: A routine reads every ticket, writes the note and the draft; you review and decide. Nothing goes out without your approval.
done.role: You stayed in charge of every word Lena received.

routineNote.title: The routine's internal note
routineNote.body: It reads the ticket, her order and the knowledge base, then leaves a note for the team: its verdict, its sources and what a person must check. Lena never sees it. Press Next once the note is in; you'll approve its reply two steps on.
routineNote.role: Your support routine works the ticket first, so you start from its findings, not from zero.

routineDraft.title: A reply draft waits for you
routineDraft.body: The routine drafts the reply to Lena, in her language. Press Next once the draft shows; you'll read it and approve it in the next step.
routineDraft.role: Nothing reaches Lena until a person says yes, and that person is you.

projects.title: Projects
projects.summary: A teammate asks for help on your task; you hand it to your agent, which breaks the work down and answers him; you review it.

home.title: Your projects
home.body: Projects and their tasks live here. Press Next.
home.role: You lead the Kestrel Field Preamp launch, one of the projects your team runs here.

myTask.title: Tobias needs your help on a launch task
myTask.body: Open the task and read his comment, then press Next.
myTask.role: You lead the Kestrel Field Preamp launch. Tobias just commented on one of its tasks and asked you for help.
myTask.way3: Open the task PREAMP-11 "Prepare the trade-show demo"
myTask.way4: Read Tobias's comment in its discussion

teammate.title: A teammate comments
teammate.body: Nothing to do yet: Tobias is about to comment on your task PREAMP-11 "Prepare the trade-show demo". Press Next once his comment is in.
teammate.role: Tobias Braun works on the launch with you, and he needs your help on one of its tasks.

askAgent.title: Hand it to your agent
askAgent.body: Write {{agent}} the request below, in your conversation with it, and press Send.
askAgent.text: Break Tobias's task PREAMP-11 "Prepare the trade-show demo" into three subtasks and create them, then reply to Tobias in its discussion. No need to check with me first.
askAgent.role: You don't have time to plan the demo units yourself. You ask {{agent}}, the way you'd ask an assistant: it splits the task and answers Tobias for you.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the task

board.title: See the whole launch at a glance
board.body: The ringed rows are the subtasks {{agent}} just made, nested under your task. Press Next.
board.role: The subtasks {{agent}} made now sit in the launch plan with everything else. Check that nothing is late.
board.way1: Click "Kestrel Field Preamp launch" at the top of the task
board.way2: You're on the project: the new subtasks are in its list

done.title: That's projects
done.body: Agents take a share of the task work; you stay in review.
done.role: Tobias has his plan, and it took you a minute, not an afternoon.

review.title: Review what it did
review.body: The task now shows its subtasks and your agent's reply to Tobias. Check, move or edit any of them, then press Next.
review.role: Before Tobias acts on the plan, you check it is the one you want.
review.way3: Check its subtasks and your agent's reply

subtasks.title: Your agent does the breakdown
subtasks.body: It reads the task and creates its subtasks. Press Next once the first one shows.
subtasks.role: While {{agent}} works, you watch the plan take shape.
subtasks.way3: Watch its steps in your conversation with it

reply.title: It answers Tobias where he asked
reply.body: Your agent posts its reply in the task's discussion. Press Next once it's there.
reply.role: Tobias gets his answer in the task's own discussion, from your agent, signed as your agent.
reply.way3: Read your agent's reply in the task's discussion

chat.title: Team chat
chat.summary: A question that needs the web; your agent researches it in its DM and cites its sources.

channels.title: Your conversations
channels.body: Channels, direct messages and your agents live in Chats. Press Next.
channels.role: You work with Tobias and the rest of the team in channels and direct messages.

question.title: A teammate has a question
question.body: Nothing to do yet: Tobias is about to ask in #battery-passport which EU battery passport rules apply from 2027. Press Next once his message is in.
question.role: Tobias is checking the battery rules for the next product, and he asks you.

readQuestion.title: Read Tobias's question
readQuestion.body: Open #battery-passport in Chats and read Tobias's message, then press Next.
readQuestion.role: Tobias needs an answer you don't have yet.

askAgent.title: Ask your agent to research it
askAgent.body: Write {{agent}} the battery passport question below, in your conversation with it, and press Send. It searches the web live and cites its sources.
askAgent.text: Which EU battery passport rules apply to us from 2027? Look it up on the web and answer in a few lines, with links to your sources.
askAgent.role: You don't know the answer, but {{agent}} can search the web and cite its sources.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the channel

searching.title: It searches the web
searching.body: {{agent}} searches the web for the battery passport rules; each tool it uses shows here as it runs. Press Next once you have seen it.
searching.role: {{agent}} does the legwork you would otherwise do in ten browser tabs.
searching.way3: Watch its steps in your conversation with it

sources.title: Its sources: the web pages it cites
sources.body: Its sources are the web pages it cites on the battery passport, shown as links under its answer. Next turns on once the answer is here.
sources.role: You can trust the answer because you can check every source yourself.
sources.way3: Read the links under its answer

followUp.title: Turn it into a task
followUp.body: In the same conversation, send the request below: type it and press Send, or press the microphone beside Send and say it. It turns the answer into a task in the launch project.
followUp.text: Please make this answer a task for Tobias in our "Kestrel Field Preamp launch" project, with the sources in its description.
followUp.role: Tobias will act on the answer, so it should become a task in the launch project.

done.title: That's chat with your agent
done.body: Your agent works across the apps from a conversation with you: it searches the web live, cites its sources and creates what you ask for. Like a person, it keeps its own memory of everything you tell it, with no compaction, and its own tools make it an expert.
done.role: Tobias has his answer with its sources, and a task to act on it, in his channel.

task.title: Your agent creates it
task.body: It creates the task, or asks you first. Press Next once it is there; you'll approve it if it asked.
task.role: {{agent}} turns its own answer into work for Tobias.

replyTobias.title: Answer Tobias in the channel
replyTobias.body: In the same conversation, send the request below with Send. {{agent}} posts the answer in #battery-passport for Tobias, signed as your agent, with its sources and the task.
replyTobias.text: Now reply to Tobias in #battery-passport: tell him what you found, with the sources, and point him to the task you created for him.
replyTobias.role: Tobias asked in the channel, so the answer belongs there, where the team sees it.

posting.title: It posts in the channel
posting.body: {{agent}} writes its answer to Tobias in #battery-passport; each step it takes shows here. Press Next once its message is in the channel.
posting.role: {{agent}} posts for you, under its own name, without you copying anything across.

replyInChannel.title: Its reply in the channel
replyInChannel.body: {{agent}}'s answer is in #battery-passport, under Tobias's question, signed as your agent. Press Next.
replyInChannel.role: Tobias has the answer, its sources and his task in one message.

sales.title: Sales
sales.summary: A prospect emails; a routine checks your CRM, reads up on them, then asks you to approve its CRM record, a quote and the reply in one request, run in order.

crm.title: Who you are talking to
crm.body: Next to a conversation, the customer card shows what your CRM knows about the sender. Press Next.
crm.role: You sell to audio companies. Before you answer anyone, you want to know who they are.
crm.way2: Open the first conversation in the inbox

routine.title: A routine for prospects
routine.body: "Research interested prospects" runs on every email from an interested prospect. It reads up on them, then prepares their CRM record, a quote and your reply, and hands all three to you to approve. It sends nothing on its own. Press Next.
routine.role: Researching each prospect by hand takes you an hour a day; a routine can do it.

enable.title: Switch it on
enable.body: Press the routine's switch to turn it on. From now on it runs on every prospect's email.
enable.role: You want every interested prospect researched before you reply, without doing it yourself.

liveEmail.title: A prospect writes in
liveEmail.body: Nothing to do yet: Inês is about to ask for a quote for 40 units. Press Next once her email is in.
liveEmail.role: Inês from Northwind Acoustics needs 40 units, and she is writing to you now.

researching.title: The routine is at work
researching.body: Wait here, nothing to do: the routine reads Inês's email, checks your CRM and, since she is new, reads her company's website. Then it prepares everything for her: her CRM record, a quote and the reply. This step moves on by itself once it is all ready.
researching.role: While the routine reads up on Inês, you do something else.

bundle.title: Nothing goes out without you
bundle.body: The routine has done its part: it read up on Inês and wrote everything, but sent nothing. What it delivers is one request in Home, named after the reply to Inês, holding the three actions it wants to take: create her CRM record, issue the quote, send the reply. Press Next.
bundle.role: Instead of three things to check one by one, you decide once.

bundleSteps.title: Three steps, in order
bundleSteps.body: The request holds three steps, run in this order, each shown in full: 1. Inês and her company as a new CRM record, with every field it writes. 2. A quote for 40 Kestrel 6 at your dealer price: its lines, discount, total and her CRM id. 3. The reply to Inês: who it goes to, the whole message, and the quote's PDF attached. What a step takes from the one before reads as that step, such as "the quote PDF from step 2". Press Next once its card is open.
bundleSteps.role: You see the whole deal before anything happens.
bundleSteps.way2: Click the request's row to open it

approve.title: Approve once
approve.body: Press Approve: the record is written (here to a fictional CRM), then the quote is issued, then the reply goes to Inês with the quote attached (here to a fictional prospect), in that order. If a step fails, nothing after it runs and the routine works out a corrected request.
approve.role: One decision, and the deal moves forward in the right order.
approve.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to keep the request waiting for you.
approve.way2: Open the request, then press Approve

brief.title: Your brief
brief.body: When it is done, the routine posts its summary in your chat with {{agent}}: who Inês is, from her company's site and your CRM, the quote's number and what went out. Press Next once it is there.
brief.role: You walk into the conversation with Inês knowing who she is.
brief.way3: Read the summary, at the bottom of the chat
brief.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the routine

card.title: What your CRM knows
card.body: The customer card now shows the CRM record you approved: Inês and Northwind Acoustics, with what the routine learned. Press Next.
card.role: The next time Inês writes, you see at once who she is.
card.way2: Open Inês's email, at the top of the inbox

done.title: That's sales
done.body: Routines do the research and keep your CRM up to date; you keep the last word on every record and every email.
done.role: Every prospect is researched before you reply, and nothing goes out without you.

commerce.title: Commerce
commerce.summary: An order arrives and its invoice issues itself; the Operations Desk answers about it and prepares the shipment for your approval.

orders.title: Your shop's orders
orders.body: Orders from your shop show here as they come in. Press Next.
orders.role: You run the shop. Orders come in all day, and each one must ship on time.

liveOrder.title: An order is coming in
liveOrder.body: Nothing to do yet: order #1097 is about to arrive, with a gift note. Press Next once it is in.
liveOrder.role: A customer is buying right now, with a gift note for the parcel.

newOrder.title: Order #1097 is in
newOrder.body: Paid, unfulfilled, with a gift note: it waits to ship. Press Next.
newOrder.role: The order lands in your list the moment the customer pays.

invoice.title: Its invoice, issued by the order
invoice.body: Its row appears here seconds after the order: the order event issued it, not an agent. Business events stay automatic. Press Next once the row is ringed.
invoice.role: The invoice for order #1097 is issued without anyone doing it.

askAgent.title: Ask the Operations Desk
askAgent.body: Write the Operations Desk the request below and press Send. It holds the shipping and invoicing tools: it checks the order and prepares the shipment for your approval.
askAgent.text: Where does order #1097 stand, and is it invoiced? Book its shipment now from its row in the shipping prep list, as it is: buy the label at the cheapest carrier offer, as one approval for me to review, and make no other change. No need to check with me first.
askAgent.role: The customer wants the parcel fast; the Operations Desk, the agent that runs shipping, can check the order and book the shipment for you.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the orders
askAgent.way2: Pick the Operations Desk under Agents

approve.title: Approve it
approve.body: Check the parcel and the carrier, then press Approve. Nothing is booked before you do.
approve.role: Nothing is booked with the carrier until you say yes.
approve.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to see the shipment come back as a draft.

done.title: That's commerce
done.body: Orders and invoices run on their own; the Operations Desk handles the judgement around them, and you approve.
done.role: Order #1097 is invoiced and shipping, and you spent a minute on it.

prepare.title: It prepares the shipment
prepare.body: The Operations Desk checks order #1097 and stages the shipment as an approval, with the gift note. Press Next once its card is there; you'll approve it next.
prepare.role: The Operations Desk does the carrier paperwork; you only check it.
prepare.way3: Watch for its card in your conversation with the Operations Desk

dev.title: Developers
dev.summary: Your agent sends a bug fix to Claude Code on a computer, and it opens a pull request.

intro.title: How Liaison codes for you
intro.body: The Liaison desktop app connects Claude Code (or Codex) on your computer to Liaison. Your agents can then send it jobs, like fixing a bug and opening a pull request. Each session runs in the mode you pick in its Modes menu. In Auto, the default, everyday commands run and risky ones wait for your yes, from anywhere. Press Next.
intro.role: You build the product's firmware, and you want bugs fixed while you do other work.

computers.title: Your connected computers
computers.body: Your connected computers show here. "Demo laptop (recorded)" is already connected in this workspace. It replays a real Claude Code session, so you install nothing. Press Next.
computers.role: A computer connected to Liaison is one your agents can send work to.

askBugs.title: Ask your agent for the recent bugs
askBugs.body: Write {{agent}} the question below, in your conversation with it, and press Send. It reads the team's Firmware bugs channel.
askBugs.text: Read the Firmware bugs channel and list the bugs reported there, newest first, one line each.
askBugs.role: Support and the test bench report bugs in a team channel. {{agent}} can read it for you.
askBugs.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen

bugs.title: The recent bugs
bugs.body: {{agent}} lists the bugs from the channel. The newest: the Kestrel 6 battery stays at 99% after a full charge. Press Next once you have read it.
bugs.role: You see what is broken without reading the whole channel.
bugs.way3: Read its answer in your conversation with it

askDispatch.title: Ask it to send the fix to the computer
askDispatch.body: Send the request below with Send. {{agent}} hands the battery bug to Claude Code on the demo laptop.
askDispatch.text: Run a fix for the battery bug stuck at 99% on my computer, the Demo laptop (recorded). It should open a pull request when done.
askDispatch.role: You pick the bug. Claude Code on your computer does the fix.

dispatch.title: The job is sent
dispatch.body: {{agent}} sends the job to Demo laptop (recorded). A session card shows up in your conversation. Wait for it, then press Next.
dispatch.role: Your agent starts the work on your computer for you. Nothing runs anywhere else.
dispatch.way3: Look for the session card in your conversation with it

stream.title: Watch it work
stream.body: The session streams what Claude Code does, step by step. Press Next once it asks for your permission; you'll allow it in the next step.
stream.role: You follow Claude Code's work as it happens, from anywhere.

permission.title: It asks first
permission.body: Pushing the fix is a risky command, so Claude Code asks you first. That is the session's mode, Auto: everyday commands run, risky ones wait for your yes. Strict, beside the model, is its sandbox: only its folder and approved websites. Press Allow once.
permission.role: The mode decides what Claude Code may run without asking, the level what it may reach. You pick both under the message box.
permission.way1: Open the demo laptop's session in the list

result.title: The result
result.body: Done: the fix is in a pull request. Its link is on the result card. Press Next.
result.role: The bug is fixed, and the change waits for your review like any other.

report.title: The report in your conversation
report.body: The finished session reports back to your conversation with {{agent}}: what it did and the pull request link. Press Next.
report.role: You hear back where you asked, without opening the session.
report.way3: Read the report in your conversation with it

pair.title: Connect your own computer
pair.body: Three steps: get the desktop app from the button here, sign in to Liaison in it, then choose Claude Code. Your computer then shows in this list, and your agents can send it jobs. Press Next.
pair.role: Your own computer can take jobs the same way.

done.title: That's development
done.body: Your agents send coding jobs to your computers, and each session asks you according to the mode you picked.
done.role: The battery bug is fixed, and the push waited for your yes.

knowledge.title: Company knowledge
knowledge.summary: Manuals, finance and playbooks in one knowledge base; each agent reads only what the person asking may open.

sources.title: Everything your company knows, in one place
sources.body: The sidebar lists the sources: resonant/manuals synced from GitLab, the Finance folder synced from Google Drive, and the documents written in Liaison. Press Next.
sources.role: You run Resonant Audio Labs. Your manuals live in GitLab, your finance files in Google Drive, your playbooks in Liaison, and all of it is here.
sources.way2: Look at the sources in the sidebar

openPl.title: Open the Q3 P&L
openPl.body: Open the Q3 2026 P&L, read the banner at its top, then press Next.
openPl.role: This file comes from the Finance folder in Google Drive. Liaison keeps it in sync and shows it read-only: edits happen in Drive.
openPl.way2: Read the banner at its top

share.title: See who can open it
share.body: Press Share and read who has access, then press Next.
share.role: Confidential means only the people it is shared with. Lucas joined support last month. He isn't on this list, so no agent he asks can open it either.
share.way1: Press Share at the top right of the document
share.way2: Read "People with access" and "Roles with access"

askAgent.title: Ask your agent across all three sources
askAgent.body: Write {{agent}} the question below, in your conversation with it, and press Send. It answers from the P&L, the manual and the playbook, and cites them.
askAgent.role: Your agent sees what you see, so it can combine the P&L, the manual and the playbook in one answer for tomorrow's board meeting.
askAgent.text: What was our gross margin in Q3, and which product drove it? Cite the documents you used.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the P&L

answer.title: Its answer, with its sources
answer.body: {{agent}} answers beside the P&L, citing the P&L, the manual and the playbook. Press Next once it has answered.
answer.role: You get one answer drawn from three places, and you can open each source.
answer.way3: Read its answer under your question

lucasAsks.title: Lucas asks the same question
lucasAsks.body: Nothing to do yet: Lucas is asking Support Desk about the Q3 gross margin in #support. Press Next once his message is in.
lucasAsks.role: Lucas joined support last month. He asks Support Desk the same thing you asked your agent.

lucasAnswer.title: Support Desk answers with his access
lucasAnswer.body: Nothing to do but read: Support Desk answers Lucas in #support, searching Knowledge as him, and the P&L is not his to open. Press Next once you have read its answer.
lucasAnswer.role: The agent works with Lucas's access, not yours, so it finds nothing.
lucasAnswer.way3: Read Support Desk's answer to Lucas

done.title: One brain, walled by role
done.body: You, Henrik in finance and any agent either of you asks can read the Q3 P&L. Lucas in support, and any agent he asks, cannot.
done.role: An agent reads with the access of the person asking it. That's why you can give agents the whole company's knowledge: nobody gets more through an agent than they could open themselves.

saasMoney.title: Subscriptions & payments
saasMoney.summary: A card fails: your agent reads Stripe, invoices and tickets, then drafts the note. You approve it.

cardFailed.title: Maison Arlon's card failed
cardFailed.role: You run Tideform. Their Visa expired, so €1,740.00 did not go through. Your agent noticed and drafted a note to Claire.
cardFailed.body: Read the highlighted row, then press Next. Nothing has gone out.

askStanding.title: Ask where you stand
askStanding.role: Before you approve, you want the whole picture: what they pay, what they are waiting for, what is on the table.
askStanding.body: Ask your agent from Chats. It reads Stripe, invoices, tickets and deals, and answers on one card.
askStanding.text: Where do we stand with Maison Arlon?
askStanding.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen

openCompany.title: One card, every app
openCompany.role: Their plan, the unpaid invoice, the open ticket and the deal for 4 more hotels, read from the apps that hold them.
openCompany.body: Read your agent's answer. Press Open on its card to see Maison Arlon's page, then press Next.
openCompany.way3: Read the answer, then press Open on its card

approveNote.title: Approve the note to Claire
approveNote.role: Élodie looks after Maison Arlon and is away: you are next in line, so the note waits on you.
approveNote.body: Open the highlighted row on Home and press Approve on its card. The note goes to Claire with a link to add a new card.
approveNote.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to take the note back before it leaves.

cardUpdated.title: Claire added a new card
cardUpdated.role: Claire read your note and added a card. Stripe tells Liaison, as it would for a real account.
cardUpdated.body: Nothing to do: the payment goes through on the new card and Stripe's page updates. Press Next once it has.

figuresMoved.title: The figures moved
figuresMoved.role: The invoice is paid, and Maison Arlon is no longer past due.
figuresMoved.body: Past due is now {{pastDue}}. MRR stays at {{mrr}}: a past due plan was counted in it all along. Both read from Stripe's mirror, as this page reads them.

saasSupport.title: Support
saasSupport.summary: A customer writes in; the support routine posts a note and a reply draft; you review and approve.

inbox.title: Your support inbox
inbox.body: Let's watch one come in: press Next.
inbox.role: You run Tideform. Every customer request lands here as a ticket, and a routine reads each one as it arrives.

liveTicket.title: A customer is writing in
liveTicket.body: Nothing to do yet: her ticket lands at the top of the list in a moment. Press Next once it is there.
liveTicket.role: Julie Ferran manages the floor at Les Tables Vauban, and shift swap notifications stopped reaching her staff after the update. She is emailing support right now.

open.title: Her ticket is here
open.body: Open her ticket, then press Next.
open.role: Before anyone answers Julie, you want to see what she wrote.
open.way2: Click Julie Ferran's ticket, at the top of the list

routineNote.title: The routine's internal note
routineNote.body: It reads the ticket, the customer's history and the help centre, then leaves a note for the team: its verdict, its sources and what a person must check. Julie never sees it. Press Next once the note is in; you'll approve its reply two steps on.
routineNote.role: Your support routine works the ticket first, so you start from its findings, not from zero.

routineDraft.title: A reply draft waits for you
routineDraft.body: The routine drafts the reply to Julie. Press Next once the draft shows; you'll read it and approve it in the next step.
routineDraft.role: Nothing reaches Julie until a person says yes, and that person is you.

approve.title: Approve the reply
approve.body: Edit a sentence if you like, then press Approve. It goes to Julie (a fictional customer here).
approve.role: You decide what goes out: read the draft as Julie will read it.
approve.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to see the reply come back as a draft.

sent.title: Sent
sent.body: The reply shows in the conversation, next to the routine's note. Press Next.
sent.role: Julie has her answer, and the team can see exactly what was said.

askAgent.title: Check how long she has been a customer
askAgent.body: Ask {{agent}} from Chats, beside the ticket, and press Send. It answers from her tickets, her company's plan and its invoices.
askAgent.text: What plan is Les Tables Vauban on, and what did Julie Ferran or her colleagues report before?
askAgent.role: Before you promise Julie a fix date, you want to know her plan and what her team reported before.

answer.title: Its answer
answer.body: {{agent}} answers beside her ticket, from the tickets and the customer's record. Press Next once it has answered.
answer.role: You decide on the fix date with her history in front of you.
answer.way3: Read its answer under your question

done.title: That's support
done.body: A routine reads every ticket, writes the note and the draft; you review and decide. Nothing goes out without your approval.
done.role: You stayed in charge of every word Julie received.

saasProjects.title: Projects
saasProjects.summary: A developer asks for help on your task; you hand it to your agent, which breaks the work down and answers him; you review it.

home.title: Your projects
home.body: Projects and their tasks live here. Press Next.
home.role: You lead the Product project, where the team plans what the rota software does next.

myTask.title: Baptiste needs your help on a task
myTask.body: Open the task and read his comment, then press Next.
myTask.role: You own the CSV rota import in the Product project. Baptiste just commented on it and asked you for help.
myTask.way3: Open the task "Import rotas from a CSV file"
myTask.way4: Read Baptiste's comment in its discussion

teammate.title: A teammate comments
teammate.body: Nothing to do yet: Baptiste is about to comment on your task "Import rotas from a CSV file". Press Next once his comment is in.
teammate.role: Baptiste Noël builds the planning engine with you, and he needs your help on this task.

askAgent.title: Hand it to your agent
askAgent.body: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the task, pick your conversation with {{agent}}, write the request below and press Send.
askAgent.text: Break Baptiste's task "Import rotas from a CSV file" into three subtasks and create them, then reply to Baptiste in its discussion. No need to check with me first.
askAgent.role: You don't have time to plan the import yourself. You ask {{agent}}, the way you'd ask an assistant: it splits the task and answers Baptiste for you.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the task

subtasks.title: Your agent does the breakdown
subtasks.body: It reads the task and creates its subtasks. Press Next once the first one shows.
subtasks.role: While {{agent}} works, you watch the plan take shape.
subtasks.way3: Watch its steps in your conversation with it

reply.title: It answers Baptiste where he asked
reply.body: Your agent posts its reply in the task's discussion. Press Next once it's there.
reply.role: Baptiste gets his answer in the task's own discussion, from your agent, signed as your agent.
reply.way3: Read your agent's reply in the task's discussion

board.title: See the whole plan at a glance
board.body: The ringed rows are the subtasks {{agent}} just made, nested under your task. Press Next.
board.role: The subtasks {{agent}} made now sit in the product plan with everything else. Check that nothing is late.
board.way1: Click "Product" at the top of the task
board.way2: You're on the project: the new subtasks are in its list

review.title: Review what it did
review.body: The task now shows its subtasks and your agent's reply to Baptiste. Check, move or edit any of them, then press Next.
review.role: Before Baptiste acts on the plan, you check it is the one you want.
review.way3: Check its subtasks and your agent's reply

done.title: That's projects
done.body: Agents take a share of the task work; you stay in review.
done.role: Baptiste has his plan, and it took you a minute, not an afternoon.

saasChat.title: Team chat
saasChat.summary: A question that needs the web; your agent researches it in its DM and cites its sources.

channels.title: Your conversations
channels.body: Channels, direct messages and your agents live in Chats. Press Next.
channels.role: You work with Lucie and the rest of the team in channels and direct messages.

question.title: A teammate has a question
question.body: Nothing to do yet: Lucie is about to ask in #seasonal-staffing how hotels plan their staff for the summer peak. Press Next once her message is in.
question.role: Lucie is planning the seasonal rota features, and she asks you.

readQuestion.title: Read Lucie's question
readQuestion.body: Open #seasonal-staffing in Chats and read Lucie's message, then press Next.
readQuestion.role: Lucie needs an answer you don't have yet.

askAgent.title: Ask your agent to research it
askAgent.body: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the channel, pick your conversation with {{agent}} and send the question below with Send. It reads the page Lucie points to and cites it. The source is a fictional page in this demo.
askAgent.text: Read the page Lucie linked in the Seasonal staffing channel and tell me in a few lines how hotels plan their seasonal staff, with the link.
askAgent.role: You don't know the answer, but {{agent}} can read the page and cite it.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the channel

searching.title: It reads the page
searching.body: {{agent}} reads the page Lucie linked; each tool it uses shows here as it runs. Press Next once you have seen it.
searching.role: {{agent}} does the legwork you would otherwise do in ten browser tabs.
searching.way3: Watch its steps in your conversation with it

sources.title: Its source: the page it cites
sources.body: Its source is the page it cites on seasonal staffing, shown as a link under its answer. The page is a fictional one made for this demo. Next turns on once the answer is here.
sources.role: You can trust the answer because you can check the source yourself.
sources.way3: Read the link under its answer

followUp.title: Turn it into a task
followUp.body: In the same conversation, send the request below: type it and press Send, or press the microphone beside Send and say it. It turns the answer into a task in the Product project.
followUp.text: Make this answer a task for Lucie in the "Product" project, with the link in its description.
followUp.role: Lucie will act on the answer, so it should become a task in the Product project.

task.title: Your agent creates it
task.body: It creates the task, or asks you first. Press Next once it is there; you'll approve it if it asked.
task.role: {{agent}} turns its own answer into work for Lucie.

posting.title: It posts in the channel
posting.body: {{agent}} writes its answer to Lucie in #seasonal-staffing; each step it takes shows here. Press Next once its message is in the channel.
posting.role: {{agent}} posts for you, under its own name, without you copying anything across.

replyInChannel.title: Its reply in the channel
replyInChannel.body: {{agent}}'s answer is in #seasonal-staffing, under Lucie's question, signed as your agent. Press Next.
replyInChannel.role: Lucie has the answer, its source and her task in one message.

done.title: That's chat with your agent
done.body: Your agent works across the apps from a conversation with you: it reads the web, cites its source and creates what you ask for. Like a person, it keeps its own memory of everything you tell it, with no compaction, and its own tools make it an expert.
done.role: Lucie has her answer with its source, and a task to act on it, in her channel.

replyTobias.title: Answer Lucie in the channel
replyTobias.body: In the same conversation, send the request below with Send. {{agent}} posts the answer in #seasonal-staffing for Lucie, signed as your agent, with its source and the task.
replyTobias.text: Reply to Lucie in #seasonal-staffing with what you found and the link, and point her to her new task.
replyTobias.role: Lucie asked in the channel, so the answer belongs there, where the team sees it.

saasSales.title: Sales
saasSales.summary: A hotel group emails; a routine checks your records, reads up on them, then asks you to approve the company, the contact, a quote and the reply in one request, run in order.

crm.title: Who you are talking to
crm.body: Next to a conversation, the customer card shows what Liaison knows about the sender. Press Next.
crm.role: You sell rota software to hotels and restaurants. Before you answer anyone, you want to know who they are.
crm.way2: Open the first conversation in the inbox

routine.title: A routine for group requests
routine.body: "Prepare quotes for group requests" runs on every email from a hotel group asking for a quote. It reads up on them, then prepares their company and contact records, a quote and your reply, and hands them to you to approve. It sends nothing on its own. Press Next.
routine.role: Researching each request by hand takes you an hour a day; a routine can do it.

enable.title: Switch it on
enable.body: Press the routine's switch to turn it on. From now on it runs on every group request.
enable.role: You want every group researched before you reply, without doing it yourself.

liveEmail.title: A group writes in
liveEmail.body: Nothing to do yet: Résidence Olympe is about to ask for a quote for 11 sites. Press Next once the email is in.
liveEmail.role: Résidence Olympe, a small hotel group, is writing to you now.

researching.title: The routine is at work
researching.body: Wait here, nothing to do: the routine reads the email, checks your records and, since the group is new, reads its website. Then it prepares everything: the company, the contact, a quote and the reply. This step moves on by itself once it is all ready.
researching.role: While the routine reads up on the group, you do something else.

bundle.title: Nothing goes out without you
bundle.body: The routine has done its part: it read up on the group and wrote everything, but sent nothing. What it delivers is one request in Home, named after its first action, holding what it wants to do: create the company, create the contact, issue the quote, send the reply. Press Next.
bundle.role: Instead of several things to check one by one, you decide once.

bundleSteps.title: Four steps, in order
bundleSteps.body: The request holds its steps, run in this order, each shown in full: 1. The company, with every field it writes. 2. The contact, linked to that company. 3. A quote for the group: its lines, total and the company it belongs to. 4. The reply to the group: who it goes to, the whole message, and the quote's PDF attached. What a step takes from the one before reads as that step. Press Next once its card is open.
bundleSteps.role: You see the whole deal before anything happens.
bundleSteps.way2: Click the request's row to open it

approve.title: Approve once
approve.body: Press Approve: the company and the contact are written, then the quote is issued, then the reply goes out with the quote attached (here to a fictional prospect), in that order. If a step fails, nothing after it runs and the routine works out a corrected request.
approve.role: One decision, and the deal moves forward in the right order.
approve.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to keep the request waiting for you.
approve.way2: Open the request, then press Approve

brief.title: Your brief
brief.body: When it is done, the routine posts its summary in your chat with {{agent}}: who the group is, from its site, the quote's number and what went out. Press Next once it is there.
brief.role: You walk into the conversation with the group knowing who they are.
brief.way3: Read the summary, at the bottom of the chat
brief.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the routine

card.title: What Liaison knows
card.body: The customer card now shows the records you approved: the contact and the company, with what the routine learned. Press Next.
card.role: The next time they write, you see at once who they are.
card.way2: Open the group's email, at the top of the inbox

done.title: That's sales
done.body: Routines do the research and keep your records up to date; you keep the last word on every record and every email.
done.role: Every group request is researched before you reply, and nothing goes out without you.

askBugs.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen

bugs.body: {{agent}} lists the bugs from the channels. The one a customer is waiting on: the payroll export stops after the fourth venue. Press Next once you have read it.
bugs.role: You see what is broken, and who is waiting, without reading the channels.
bugs.way3: Read its answer in your conversation with it

result.role: The export is fixed, and the change waits for your review like any other.

report.title: The report in your conversation
report.body: The finished session reports back to your conversation with {{agent}}: what it did and the pull request link. Press Next.
report.role: You hear back where you asked, without opening the session.
report.way3: Read the report in your conversation with it

askTell.title: Tell the customer
askTell.body: Send the request below with Send. {{agent}} drafts the reply to the customer whose ticket this was; it waits for your approval.
askTell.text: Draft a reply to Claire on her payroll export ticket saying where the fix stands, with the pull request link if there is one. Don't send it, I want to read it first.
askTell.role: The ticket, the fix and the customer are one thread. Your agent can close it.
askTell.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the session

replyDraft.title: A reply draft waits
replyDraft.body: {{agent}} drafts the reply on her ticket. Press Next once its card shows; you'll read it and approve it in the next step.
replyDraft.role: Nothing reaches Claire until a person says yes.
replyDraft.way3: Look for the reply's card in your conversation with it

approveReply.title: Approve the reply
approveReply.body: Read the draft as Claire will read it, then press Approve. It goes to Claire (a fictional customer here).
approveReply.role: The customer hears from you once the fix exists, not before.
approveReply.undo: Let it go, or press Undo to see the reply come back as a draft.

pair.title: Connect your own computer
pair.body: Three steps: get the desktop app from the button here, sign in to Liaison in it, then choose Claude Code. Your computer then shows in this list, and your agents can send it jobs. Press Next.
pair.role: Your own computer can take jobs the same way.

done.title: That's development
done.body: Your agents send coding jobs to your computers, and each session asks you according to the mode you picked. The ticket, the fix and the customer told are one thread.
done.role: The export is fixed, the customer is told, and the push waited for your yes.

saasKnowledge.title: Company knowledge
saasKnowledge.summary: Help articles, policies and playbooks in one knowledge base; each agent reads only what the person asking may open.

sources.title: Everything your company knows, in one place
sources.body: The sidebar lists the collections: the help centre, the finance policies and the product documents written in Liaison. Press Next.
sources.role: You run Tideform. Your help articles, your pricing and your finance policies are all here, and who may read what is set per document.
sources.way2: Look at the collections in the sidebar

openPl.title: Open the refund policy
openPl.body: Open the Refund policy, read it, then press Next.
openPl.role: This policy belongs to finance: it says when a charge is refunded and who approves it.
openPl.way2: Read the top of the document

share.title: See who can open it
share.body: Press Share and read who has access, then press Next.
share.role: Restricted means only the people it is shared with. Clémence joined support last month. She isn't on this list, so no agent she asks can open it either.
share.way1: Press Share at the top right of the document
share.way2: Read "People with access" and "Roles with access"

askAgent.title: Ask your agent across the sources
askAgent.body: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the policy, pick your conversation with {{agent}} and send the question below with Send. It answers from the refund policy and the failed payments article, and cites them.
askAgent.role: Your agent sees what you see, so it can combine two policies in one answer.
askAgent.text: When do we refund a charge, who approves it, and what happens to a card that failed? Cite the documents you used.
askAgent.way1: Open Chats at the bottom of the screen, beside the policy

answer.title: Its answer, with its sources
answer.body: {{agent}} answers beside the policy, citing both documents. Press Next once it has answered.
answer.role: You get one answer drawn from two places, and you can open each source.
answer.way3: Read its answer under your question

lucasAsks.title: Clémence asks the same question
lucasAsks.body: Nothing to do yet: Clémence is asking Support Desk about refunds in #support. Press Next once her message is in.
lucasAsks.role: Clémence joined support last month. She asks Support Desk what you asked your agent.

lucasAnswer.title: Support Desk answers with her access
lucasAnswer.body: Nothing to do but read: Support Desk answers Clémence in #support, searching Knowledge as her, and the refund policy is not hers to open. Press Next once you have read its answer.
lucasAnswer.role: The agent works with Clémence's access, not yours, so it finds nothing about refunds.
lucasAnswer.way3: Read Support Desk's answer to Clémence

done.title: One brain, walled by role
done.body: You, Sara in finance and any agent either of you asks can read the refund policy. Clémence in support, and any agent she asks, cannot.
done.role: An agent reads with the access of the person asking it. That's why you can give agents the whole company's knowledge: nobody gets more through an agent than they could open themselves.
